python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
parts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(t)
 parts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n'+t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(parts))
print(''.join(parts)[:29000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
for f in p.iterdir():
 if f.name == 'manuscript.txt' or (f.name.startswith('page-') and f.suffix in ('.txt','.png')):
  f.unlink()
p.rmdir()
print('Removed temporary PDF extracts and renders.')
PY"

strengths: The mean-point correspondence is a simple, useful contribution to geometric vision. It converts a difficult four-point/three-view estimation problem into calls to established five-point and P3P solvers. Approximating one correspondence permits substantially more flexibility than imposing an affine camera model throughout the first two views.

The empirical support is extensive: 90,000 camera triplets across 18 scenes and three datasets, evaluations in PoseLib and GC-RANSAC, synthetic geometry and noise experiments, and ablations of perturbation, refinement, filtering, and early non-minimal refitting. Supplementary results also evaluate all three camera pairs, addressing a limitation of the main pose metric.

Table 2 demonstrates practical value even against the strengthened five-point baseline. On PhotoTourism, 4p3v(M)+R+F+ENM achieves essentially identical AUC@10 to 5pt+P3P+R+F+ENM (76.16 versus 76.20) with lower reported runtime (44.51 versus 56.52 ms). The perturbed mean-point variants further improve accuracy. These results support acceptance independently of the comparison with homotopy continuation.

The modular method is explained clearly, and the manuscript acknowledges its approximate nature and dependence on local optimization. Validation on a held-out scene, reported implementation settings, standard solver components, and a source-code link support reproducibility. The main originality is concentrated in the mean-point construction and its effective integration into robust three-view estimation.
weaknesses: The runtime comparison with homotopy continuation has a consequential confound. Section 8.3 reports approximately 45 ms of data/weight loading per RANSAC invocation, which is substantial relative to the 60–67 ms total HC runtimes in Table 2. Reusing the loaded model across triplets could materially change the comparison. Table 4 also reports lower individual solver latency for HC (66.06 microseconds) than for M (83.92) or M±δ (218.71). The reported experiments therefore do not establish a general steady-state speed advantage over HC.

The strongest accuracy gains over an equally enhanced five-point baseline are modest and sometimes expensive. On PhotoTourism, M±δ+R+F+ENM improves AUC@10 from 76.20 to 77.14 while increasing runtime from 56.52 to 112.60 ms. Although Table 2 appropriately includes the enhanced baseline, Figure 4's trade-off curves and Table 5's alternative-metric comparison omit its +R+F variants. This limits the evidence for the broad claim of the best speed–accuracy trade-off.

The geometric bound offers limited support for general pose robustness. Lemma 1 bounds the artificial correspondence's point-to-epipolar-line distance by the image triangle's extent; it does not bound the recovered pose error or establish convergence of ENM/LM. Figure 9 shows residual approximation error even for noiseless data, and Table 2 demonstrates the affine solver's strong dependence on ENM. The statement that ENM makes scene dependence negligible should consequently be restricted to the evaluated configurations.
